# Building a Procedural Hex Map with Wave Function Collapse

In the realm of game development, procedural generation has emerged as a captivating technique for creating diverse and engaging environments. One of the latest innovations in this field is a procedural hex map generator that employs Wave Function Collapse (WFC) to craft unique medieval island worlds. This project, developed using WebGPU and backtracking techniques, has garnered attention for its ability to produce stunning landscapes in a matter of seconds.

## The Inspiration Behind the Project

The creator, inspired by the procedural maps from classic games like Advanced Dungeons & Dragons, sought to recreate the thrill of exploration in a digital format. The generator constructs maps using a staggering 4,100 hex tiles, each defined by various terrain features such as grass, water, and roads. The result is a vast array of possibilities, with each map being unique, seeded, and deterministic.

## Understanding Wave Function Collapse

At the heart of this project lies the Wave Function Collapse algorithm, initially developed by Maxim Gumin. WFC is akin to the popular board game Carcassonne, where tiles must match at their edges. The hexagonal tiles in this project have six edges, which significantly increases the complexity compared to traditional square tiles. Each tile can exist in one of 900 possible states—thanks to its six rotations and five elevation levels—making the generation process both intricate and fascinating.

### How the WFC Process Works

The WFC process begins with a superposition of all possible tiles for each cell, followed by the selection of the most constrained cell, which is then collapsed into one of its valid states. The algorithm propagates constraints to neighboring cells based on matching edges, repeating this process until all cells are resolved or a dead end is reached. Notably, the implementation includes a modular WFC system that divides the map into 19 hexagonal grids to manage complexity effectively.

## Addressing Challenges with Backtracking

As with any complex algorithm, challenges arise, particularly with larger grids that may lead to unsolvable configurations. To tackle these issues, backtracking is employed, allowing the generator to undo decisions and explore alternative paths. A layered recovery system enhances this backtracking mechanism, ensuring a more robust solution to conflicts that may arise during the tile placement process.

## Elevation and Visual Aesthetics

One of the standout features of this map generator is its incorporation of 3D elevation, introducing five distinct levels that add depth to the terrain. The visual quality is further enhanced through post-processing techniques like ambient occlusion and dynamic shadow mapping. Moreover, the use of natural debug colors aids in visualizing elevation and tile placement, making the debugging process more intuitive.

## Optimizing for Performance

Performance is a critical consideration in any interactive application. This project utilizes BatchedMesh for efficient rendering, minimizing draw calls and maintaining smooth performance. While the demo runs efficiently on mobile devices, some users have reported performance issues on certain laptops, prompting discussions about optimizing graphics settings and potential software rendering limitations.

title: Velxio, Arduino Emulator
description: Velxio is a groundbreaking free, open-source Arduino emulator that enables users to write, compile, and simulate Arduino code directly in their web browsers, eliminating the need for extensive installations or cloud dependencies. This powerful tool features real-time simulation, interactive electronic components, and advanced code editing capabilities, making it an ideal resource for hobbyists, educators, and developers alike. With support for a variety of protocols and the ability to produce real executable files, Velxio is set to transform how users engage with embedded systems.
